h1:
Nonthaburi Riverside Restaurants
An Easy Evening by the Water
intro: Nonthaburi has something Bangkok folks tend to forget about: a stretch of the Chao Phraya that still feels open and quieter than it does downtown. As the light softens in the late afternoon, the riverside spots around Pak Kret, Sanambinnam, and on toward Tha Nam Non start switching on their lights, a cool breeze comes up off the water, and express boats and tugboats drift past in a steady rhythm. We picked 8 places where the seats are comfortable, the view is real, and the food actually delivers.

blocks.html: The charm of Nonthaburi's riverside spots is that they're not as packed as Asiatique or the Charoen Nakhon side. The river here is wide, curves nicely, and Koh Kret sits in the middle to give the view some depth. Many of these places are old wooden houses or converted rice mills, and a few run their own boats across from the opposite pier. The sweet spot is 16:30–18:30, when the sun is going down and the sky shifts color, then you can settle in and stay for the live music.

items.name: The River House 1953
items.blurb: A wooden riverside house in the Sanambinnam area (Soi Nonthaburi 17) that has been reworked from an old home into a comfortable place to sit, with a garden zone, a railing-side riverfront zone, and private rooms. The view is open enough to catch the sunset. The dishes people order most are salt-grilled river prawns, clear-broth tom yum with fish, and young-coconut sago to finish. Live music in the evening.

items.name: Baan Rabieng Nam
items.blurb: Tucked down a deep soi in the Sanambinnam area (Soi Nonthaburi 23), decorated like an old wooden house set in a shady garden, with a golf cart and boat to shuttle you in. The food is honest, home-style Thai — standouts are crab curry with sea blite, steamed seafood curry (hor mok), and river prawns. It's quiet, the breeze is cool, and it's a good spot to settle in for a while and listen to the live music.

items.name: Tara River Terrace
items.blurb: The big draw here is the location right across from Koh Kret, with a clear view of the leaning chedi at Wat Poramaiyikawat. The riverside tables are open to the breeze, and there's an air-conditioned zone too. Signature dishes include jungle curry, garlic-fried fish, fried squid with roe, and tom yum. Pairs well with a walk around Koh Kret on the same day.
items.meta: Pak Kret (across from Koh Kret) · Open 11:00–22:30

items.name: Song Fang Khlong Riverside
items.blurb: A Pak Kret spot designed to feel airy and open, with a calm, quiet riverside view. The selling point is the free swan-boat pedaling for kids and live music in the evening. It opens from late afternoon into the night, so it's good for an after-work wind-down by the water. The menu is Thai plus fried snacks, and the house dessert is the Song Fang Khlong ice cream.
items.meta: Pak Kret · Open 16:00–23:00 · Free swan boats

items.name: Moon River
items.blurb: A Thai–fusion riverside spot looking across at the Nonthaburi town side. There are several zones, including an upper floor with an open view, and the mood leans romantic — good for couples or a special meal. You'll find Thai food, seafood, and wood-fired pizza, plus live music in the evening. Parking is limited, so come before early evening.
items.meta: Chao Phraya riverside, Nonthaburi town side · Open Tue–Sun 11:00–22:00

items.name: Samsen Villa Live the River
items.blurb: A long-running spot on the Chao Phraya with an easygoing feel and live music every evening. The standout is a private boat cruise with dinner for groups who want something a bit special. The menu is Thai and seafood, and the fried German pork knuckle is a frequent order. Good for groups or events.
items.meta: Chao Phraya riverside · Open evenings 16:00–23:00 · Boat cruise available

items.name: Krua Ja Yan 2 River Fish
items.blurb: A casual home-style cook-to-order place by the water, focused on fresh river fish. Standouts are river-fish tom yum, sour curry with fish roe, and fish cakes. Prices are easy on the wallet, and while it isn't fancy, the breeze is good and the view is real — a great spot to eat your fill without dressing up. Closed Monday, with both free and paid parking.

items.name: Siam 77
items.blurb: A vintage-style wooden house by the water under the Rama V Bridge. The riverside tables look out on the bridge as a backdrop, which is lovely once the lights come on. Signature dishes are spicy fish salad, river prawns, and garlic-fried fish. The entrance is down a narrow soi, so use the restaurant's shuttle or ask about parking before you go.
items.meta: Under the Rama V Bridge · Open 10:00–24:00

blocks.title: When the Breeze Is Best
blocks.html: If you want both the sunset and the cool breeze, book or arrive before 17:00 to grab a railing-side table, then settle in until evening. The waterfront tables at the popular spots fill up fast from Friday to Sunday.

blocks.text: How to Pick the Right Spot for the Meal You Want

items: A date / special meal — Moon River or The River House 1953: open views, a calm mood, good for photos and lingering over conversation.
A family with kids — Song Fang Khlong Riverside has free swan boats so the kids stay busy while the adults relax with the live music.
Fresh river fish at a good price — Krua Ja Yan 2 is straightforward and filling without costing much.
Pairing with a Koh Kret day trip — Tara River Terrace sits right across from the island, so you can see the leaning chedi while you eat.
A big group / event — Samsen Villa Live the River has plenty of tables and a boat cruise.

blocks.text: Getting There and What to Know

blocks.html: The Sanambinnam and Tha Nam Non areas are easy to reach on the MRT Purple Line — get off at Yaek Tiwanon or Phra Nang Klao Bridge, then take a short ride. For the Pak Kret side and the spots across from Koh Kret, driving yourself is more convenient since the parking is roomier. Some places down deep sois, like Baan Rabieng Nam or Siam 77, run a boat or shuttle from a drop-off point, so call ahead to check what time the last shuttle runs.

blocks.title: Check Before You Go
blocks.html: Many riverside spots adjust their opening hours and closing days with the seasons and the tides, especially in the rainy season when the water runs high — some waterfront tables may be off-limits then. We'd call to book and ask about parking in advance.

items.name: Come early to beat traffic
items.blurb: Leave town to reach the restaurant before 17:00 — you get the sunset and skip the bridge jam at the end of the workday.

items.name: Bring a light jacket
items.blurb: After sunset the breeze off the river is cooler than you'd expect, and the railing-side tables get gusty.

faq.q: Which Nonthaburi riverside restaurant has the best view for the sunset?
faq.a: The spots with the most open sunset views are The River House 1953 and Moon River — both have riverside tables facing the evening light. Arrive before 17:00 to grab a railing-side table.

faq.q: Which spots are best for watching the boats and hearing live music?
faq.a: Several have live music in the evening, like Baan Rabieng Nam, Song Fang Khlong Riverside, and Samsen Villa Live the River. Sitting right on the water means you'll see express boats and tugboats passing by every so often.

faq.q: Roughly how much do Nonthaburi riverside restaurants cost per person?
faq.a: Most run around ฿250–600 per person depending on how much seafood or river fish you order. Casual spots like Krua Ja Yan 2 keep it to around ฿200–400 per person.

faq.q: Can I get to the Nonthaburi riverside spots by public transport?
faq.a: The Sanambinnam and Tha Nam Non areas are reachable on the MRT Purple Line — get off at Yaek Tiwanon or Phra Nang Klao Bridge, then take a short ride. For the Pak Kret side and across from Koh Kret, driving yourself is easier since parking is roomier.

faq.q: What time of year should I avoid the waterfront tables?
faq.a: In the rainy season when the water runs high (roughly September–November), some places may close their waterfront tables or change their hours. Call to check before you head out.
